cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, about the Midianites, the people the LORD said had deceived Israel in the matter of Peor (Numbers 25:16-18). He gives Moses an assignment: "Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites." And then, friend, He tells Moses something about Moses himself.

cards.question: After Moses takes vengeance on the Midianites, what does the LORD say will happen to him?

answers.text: He will be gathered to his people
He will cross over the Jordan
He will be made king of Israel

cards.text: So Moses tells the people to arm some of their men to go execute the LORD's vengeance on Midian. Not the whole camp, though. He's got a number in mind.

cards.question: Moses says to send ___ men from each tribe of Israel into battle.
A thousand men from each tribe of Israel makes an army of twelve thousand armed for war.

cards.text: Moses sends them into battle, and with them goes Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest. Phinehas doesn't show up empty-handed.

cards.question: What does Phinehas take with him into battle?

answers.text: The sanctuary vessels and signal trumpets
The ark of the covenant and Aaron's staff
The priestly robes and the anointing oil

cards.text: They wage war against Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they kill every male, including Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian. And hold on, friend, because there's one more name on that list.

cards.question: Besides the five kings of Midian, who else is killed with the sword?

cards.text: That's Balaam, the man Balak king of Moab once called to curse Israel (Numbers 22:4-6). And the Israelites capture the Midianite women and their children and plunder all their herds, flocks and goods.

cards.question: With the people and goods taken, the Israelites ___ all the cities and encampments where the Midianites had lived.
The army carries away all the plunder, both people and animals, and brings it to Moses, Eleazar the priest and the congregation of Israel.

cards.text: Moses, Eleazar the priest and all the leaders head outside the camp on the plains of Moab to meet the army. But friend, this is no welcome-home party, because Moses is angry with the officers, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds.

cards.question: Moses is angry with the army's officers. What does he ask them?

answers.text: If they spared all the women
Why they killed the five kings
Where Phinehas had gone off to

cards.text: Moses points back to Peor, in Numbers 25. He says these women, through the counsel of Balaam, caused the sons of Israel to turn unfaithfully against the LORD.

cards.question: Moses says that because of what happened at Peor, a ___ struck the congregation of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses gives an order that's hard to read, friend, and I'm not going to soften it: kill all the boys, and every woman who has had relations with a man. Every girl who never has is to be spared.
The soldiers are back from Midian, but they can't just stroll into camp. Moses says anyone who has killed a person or touched the dead has to stay outside the camp first.

cards.question: Moses says anyone who has killed a person or touched the dead must stay outside the camp for ___ days.
On the third day and the seventh day, the soldiers purify themselves and their captives too.

cards.text: Moses puts every garment, leather good, goat's hair item and wooden article on the cleanup list, so this isn't laundry day, friend, this is laundry WEEK. Then Eleazar the priest shares the LORD's statute for the gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin and lead.

cards.question: Eleazar says the metal that can withstand the fire is made clean how?

answers.text: It is buried for seven days
It is offered on the altar

cards.question: Eleazar says everything that can't withstand the fire must pass through the water.

cards.text: Even the fireproof metal still gets the water of purification, and on the seventh day the soldiers wash their clothes and come back into camp clean. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer under the dust, and NOBODY ever offered me a deal like that.
Then the LORD tells Moses, Eleazar the priest and the family heads to count everything captured, both people and animals. After that, they're to divide it into two halves.

cards.question: The LORD says to divide the captives between the ___ who went out to battle and the rest of the ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses to set aside one out of every five hundred from the soldiers' half for Eleazar the priest as the LORD's tribute, and one out of every fifty from the congregation's half for the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle. Friend, I lose count of the sprinkles on ONE cookie, and Moses has to keep all these numbers straight.

Moses and Eleazar do as the LORD commanded and count it all: 675,000 sheep, 72,000 cattle, 61,000 donkeys and 32,000 women. They split it in half, with the LORD's tribute and the Levites' share set aside, just as the LORD said.

Then the commanders of thousands and of hundreds come to Moses, and friend, the last time he met these officers, he was angry with them. This time they've counted every soldier under their command, and I bet they counted TWICE.

cards.question: After counting the soldiers under their command, the commanders report that not one of them is missing.
The commanders bring the LORD an offering of the gold each man acquired. What do they say it's for?

answers.text: To pay for the army's weapons
To thank Moses for leading them

cards.text: Moses and Eleazar receive all the gold articles, and they weigh 16,750 shekels, which is a LOT of gold for a stamper who came with a price sticker that said 25 cents. And the text adds that each of the soldiers had taken plunder for himself.

cards.question: Where do Moses and Eleazar bring the commanders' gold, as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD?

answers.text: Up to the top of Mount Nebo
Across to the city of Jericho

findings.problem: Discovery questions recur too often rather than remaining occasional. In stop 1, cards 2, 4, 7, 9 and 16 give no earlier-card basis for inferring Moses' future, the exact number from each tribe, Phinehas' equipment, the additional man killed, or the judgment at Peor. Stop 2 cards 2 and 3 likewise ask for the seven-day period and purification schedule without contextual clues. These choices repeatedly rely on luck or prior Bible knowledge instead of reasoning from the setups.

rule.text: Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
